question: Does the popular claim that 97% of scientists agree on human-caused climate change accurately represent Cook et al 2013, whose 97.1% figure covers only the abstracts that expressed a position on AGW?

claim_atoms.text: In Cook et al (2013), the 97.1% consensus figure is the endorsement rate among only the abstracts that expressed a position on AGW, while 66.4% of the 11 944 abstracts expressed no position; the popular 'X% of scientists agree' restatement omits that denominator.

66.4% of abstracts expressed no position on AGW

credential-free HTTPS retrieval of the archived version-of-record PDF
endorsement expressed in abstract text, not a survey of scientists' personal views

results.interpretation: The headline number is real but conditional: it describes the roughly one-third of abstracts that took a position, not all abstracts or all scientists. Restatements that drop the 'expressing a position' qualifier overstate the measured base.
results.proposition: In Cook et al (2013), the 97.1% consensus figure is the endorsement rate among only the abstracts that expressed a position on AGW, while 66.4% of the 11 944 abstracts expressed no position; the popular 'X% of scientists agree' restatement omits that denominator.

results.uncertainty: Scope limited to one primary source and its abstract-rating phase; the study measures positions expressed in abstracts, not scientists' private views, and popular restatements vary in wording.
results.warrant: The abstract states the 97.1% figure applies to abstracts expressing a position and separately reports 66.4% expressed no position; Table 3 counts reproduce 97.1% among position-takers.

scope.comparison_target: The popular restatement '97% of scientists agree' versus what Cook et al (2013) actually measured.
scope.excluded: Other consensus studies, opinion surveys of scientists, and the underlying merits of AGW itself.
scope.included: The public primary source Cook et al (2013) and the exact figures it reports for abstract ratings.
